planting.note: Plant a container or balled shrub in early spring or fall; this hybrid flowers heavily before leaf-out.

directions: Site this multi-stemmed hybrid serviceberry where its dense spring flower display and clean habit can be appreciated, in well-drained soil that stays evenly moist through establishment. It tolerates light shade but flowers and fruits best with several hours of direct sun. Prune only to remove crossing or damaged wood right after flowering, since it blooms on old wood. The small summer berries draw birds quickly, so net branches if you want to harvest any yourself.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit records

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings in spring; needs a male pollinator nearby for fruit set.

directions: This dwarf, dense-growing selection stays low and spreading, making it a practical choice for a compact coastal or windbreak hedge where a full-size sea buckthorn would be too large. Plant in lean, sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates salt spray and poor fertility but resents waterlogging. Because the species is dioecious, keep a male plant within pollinating distance if you want the orange berries to form. Shear lightly after fruiting if a tighter hedge form is desired.
